captive_summary: Okinawa Electric's 35,000 kW Yoshinoura Multi-Gas-Turbine plant (commissioned Mar 20 2015, LNG-primary multi-fuel) has FOUR documented duties: (1) island-wide blackstart power if all of Okinawa loses power, (2) explicit security/backup power ("保安電源") for the LNG fuel tank at Yoshinoura thermal power station when that station loses power, (3) peak-demand response power in normal operation, and (4) BOG processing. Duty (3) means it carries real load in normal service, and duty (2) directly powers/secures the LNG terminal's own tank systems, so this is captive power under the SOP — category power_generation per the 'carries load in service' rule (not standby_backup) given its normal peak-power duty.
confirmed_how: Japanese Wikipedia's article on Yoshinoura Thermal Power Station states the Multi-Gas-Turbine plant serves as "系統立上げ電源" (grid blackstart), as "吉の浦火力発電所LNG燃料タンクの保安電源" (security power for the Yoshinoura power station's LNG fuel tank), and as "通常時の電力ピーク対応電源" (normal-time peak-demand power). Okinawa Electric's own Mar 20 2015 commissioning press release (via itmedia/SmartJapan) independently confirms the same four purposes verbatim, including the LNG-tank security-power role and BOG処理機能 (BOG processing capability).
